def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses.title: Forward-sector hypotheses for a simple state domain

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, §§III.A–III.B
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapters 2 and 4, complete 607-page edition

def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses.statement:
Let $P$ be a set of primitive type labels. A formal type $\Gamma$ records a finitely supported amount function $\nu_\Gamma:P\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$, not identically zero. Primitive generators have their unit amount function. Positive scaling, separated product, and thermal-join constructors retain distinct formal tags and obey

$$\nu_{s\Gamma}=s\nu_\Gamma,\qquad \nu_{\Gamma\otimes\Gamma'}=\nu_\Gamma+\nu_{\Gamma'}\qquad(s>0).$$

Separated and joined types are distinct constructors even when their amount functions agree. Permutation, reassociation, and scaled-splitting conventions preserve the amount function. Define the positive **bookkeeping weight** $w_\Gamma:=\sum_{p\in P}\nu_\Gamma(p)$, a finite sum over support. Thus $w_{s\Gamma}=s w_\Gamma$ and every product or join has weight $w_\Gamma+w_{\Gamma'}$. The optional empty unit has zero amount function and weight zero; it is represented only by the empty compound, not as a simple chart. These are formal amounts, not masses in kilograms or an empirical conservation law. The functions and pointwise operations use [[def-function-space]]; their finite-support convention and finite sums are those of [[def-tdmath-tagged-scalable-compound]] and [[lem-tdmath-compound-mass-well-defined]].

Let $I$ index the declared family of simple types $\Gamma_i$. For each simple type $\Gamma$ in that family, let $n_\Gamma\ge1$ and let $\Gamma\subset\mathbb R^{n_\Gamma+1}$ be nonempty, open and convex, with coordinates $x=(u,v)$. The notation for a type and its chart is shared, but each state has a distinct raw tag $(\Gamma,x)$. Scaled charts are distinct tagged copies $s\Gamma=\{sx:x\in\Gamma\}$ with coordinate transport $x\mapsto sx$; transported raw tags remain distinct from the original raw tags. Let $e_{(\Gamma,x)}$ be the unit point mass from [[def-tdmath-tagged-scalable-compound]]. The represented state is

$$\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x):=w_\Gamma e_{(\Gamma,x)},\qquad m(\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x))=w_\Gamma.$$

Write $\mathsf{J}(x):=\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)$ when $x$ already carries its type tag. All state notation in this framework's compound comparisons, including a bare $x$, denotes $\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)$; a raw unit point mass is always written $e_{(\Gamma,x)}$. A separated pair is addition of represented states, not a unit product tag. Nonnegative multiples are pointwise and zero terms are omitted. For an encoded compound $c$, its aggregate composition is the finite amount function

$$\nu(c):=\sum_{(\Gamma,x)\in\operatorname{supp}(c)}\frac{c(\Gamma,x)}{w_\Gamma}\nu_\Gamma;\qquad m(c)=\sum_{p\in P}\nu(c)(p).$$

Fix the formal interpretation $\Pi(c)$ as the finite separated preparation whose factor at each nonzero raw tag $(\Gamma,x)$ is the amount $c(\Gamma,x)/w_\Gamma$ of that typed state, using the declared coordinate scaling transport. The accessibility relation on coefficient maps is the pullback of the declared relation on these preparations. Merging or splitting repeated copies of the same preparation is reversible; permutation and reassociation preserve the preparation. Thus $\Pi(\mathsf{J}_{s\Gamma}(sx))$ and $\Pi(s\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x))$ are the same declared scaled preparation and yield

$$\mathsf{J}_{s\Gamma}(sx)\sim s\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x),$$

although their raw point masses have different tags and are not equal. This reversible transport commutes with finite composition, nested type constructors, and scaled splitting. It is part of the precise formal scaling interpretation, not a deduction about physical accessibility from coordinate multiplication. A physical use must adopt the stated preparation maps and accessibility assumptions; fixed-composition models compare only preparations with the same $\nu$, while a declared channel model may additionally compare different compositions of equal $m$.

A comparison $A\prec B$ is defined only when $m(A)=m(B)$, as in the coefficient-map supplier. Write $A\sim B$ when both directions hold, and $A\prec\prec B$ when only the forward direction holds. On any fixed simple type, dividing every represented state by the same positive constant $w_\Gamma$ gives its unit-point-mass comparison. Positive scaling and its inverse preserve and reflect order; whenever the required CH and reference hypotheses hold, the unit-state entropy theorem applies after that normalization. If $S$ represents unit-point-mass comparisons, the entropy of a represented state is $w_\Gamma S(x)$ and the entropy of a finite sum $\sum_j t_j\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x_j)$ is $\sum_j t_j w_\Gamma S(x_j)$. No independent rescaling across different types is assumed without a calibrator.

The common relation satisfies A1–A6 on all equal-mass finite compounds: (A1) reflexivity; (A2) transitivity; (A3) if $A\prec B$, then $A+C\prec B+C$ for every compound $C$; (A4) if $A\prec B$, then $tA\prec tB$ for every $t>0$; (A5) $t\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)$ is equivalent to $s\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)+(t-s)\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)$ for $t>0$ and $0<s<t$, with the reversible scaled-copy transport above; (A6) for equal-mass $A,B$, fixed positive equal-mass spectators $Z_0,Z_1$, and every sequence $\epsilon_n>0$ decreasing to zero, $A+\epsilon_n Z_0\prec B+\epsilon_n Z_1$ for all $n$ implies $A\prec B$. These are hypotheses, not conclusions. No comparison hypothesis is included here.

For each $i$ and $x\in\Gamma_i$, define the forward sector $A_x:=\{y\in\Gamma_i:\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(x)\prec\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(y)\}$. The simple-domain assumptions are: (A7) for $x,y\in\Gamma_i$ and $0<t<1$, the encoded compound $t\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(x)+(1-t)\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(y)$ compares to $\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(tx+(1-t)y)$; both have bookkeeping mass $w_{\Gamma_i}$, and convexity puts the recombined coordinate in the chart; (S1) each $x$ has a strict successor; (S2) $A_x$ has exactly one supporting hyperplane at $x$, expressible as $u-u_x+P_i(x)\cdot(v-v_x)=0$ with finite slope $P_i(x)$, and $P_i$ is locally Lipschitz; (S3) the boundary of $A_x$ relative to $\Gamma_i$ is arcwise connected. A supporting hyperplane means that $A_x$ lies in one of its closed half-spaces and meets the plane at $x$. The affine hull is the smallest affine subspace containing a set; relative interior is interior in that affine hull. Closure and boundary are taken in the indicated affine hull or in $\Gamma_i$, as named; boundary is closure intersected with closure of the complement in that relative topology.

This definition imposes no physical interpretation, units, or empirical claim. A contact theorem that uses joins must separately assume that each join is a simple domain satisfying these same forward-sector hypotheses.

def-tdmath-thermal-contact-hypotheses.title: Thermal joins and conditional contact hypotheses

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, §IV.A, pp. 51–54
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapters 2 and 4, complete 607-page edition

def-tdmath-thermal-contact-hypotheses.statement:
For two simple domains $\Gamma_i\subset\mathbb R^{n_i+1}$ and $\Gamma_j\subset\mathbb R^{n_j+1}$, write their coordinates $(u_i,v_i)$ and $(u_j,v_j)$. Their thermal-join domain is

$$\Delta_{ij}:=\{(u,v_i,v_j):\exists u_i,u_j,\ (u_i,v_i)\in\Gamma_i,\ (u_j,v_j)\in\Gamma_j,\ u=u_i+u_j\}.$$

The joined simple type is a distinct formal tag with amount function $\nu_{\Delta_{ij}}=\nu_{\Gamma_i}+\nu_{\Gamma_j}$ and weight $w_{\Delta_{ij}}=w_{\Gamma_i}+w_{\Gamma_j}$, as defined in [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]]. Encode the separated pair by $\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(x)+\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_j}(y)$ and a joined coordinate $Z$ by $\mathsf{J}_{\Delta_{ij}}(Z)$. Their bookkeeping masses agree, and their aggregate composition functions agree. These encoded maps and their raw tags remain distinct. Positive coordinate-scaled copies use the reversible preparation transport of that definition; nested joins preserve their finite primitive amount function under reassociation and permutation. The empty type contributes the zero map.

Write $J_{ij}(x,y)$ for the join state with the summed energy coordinate and the unchanged work coordinates. A compound pair $(x,y)$ and $J_{ij}(x,y)$ have the same total energy and work coordinates but are distinct tagged objects. Define $x\sim_T y$ exactly when $\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(x)+\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_j}(y)$ and $\mathsf{J}_{\Delta_{ij}}(J_{ij}(x,y))$ are accessible in both directions. Nested joins use the declared reassociation and permutation identifications.

Assume every finite join is itself a simple domain satisfying [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]]. The contact hypotheses are mathematical assumptions on the common relation: (T1) $(x,y)\prec J_{ij}(x,y)$; (T2) every join state has at least one reversible split into component states at its stated coordinates, and the equal-state split of any state into positive scaled copies of itself is reversible; (T3) $\sim_T$ is transitive; (T4) for every simple state $x$ there are states $x_0,x_1$ in its domain with $x_0\prec\prec x\prec\prec x_1$ and $x_0\sim_T x_1$; (T5) for every ordered pair of simple systems, every $x$ in the first and every work coordinate $v$ in the second's projection $\rho(\Gamma_j):=\{v:\exists u,(u,v)\in\Gamma_j\}$, there is a state $y$ with work coordinate $v$ and $x\sim_T y$.

For the completed calibrator branch, add (C1) **join coherence**: whenever $x\sim_T y$, the join state $J_{ij}(x,y)$ is thermally equivalent to each of $x$ and $y$ under the nested-join identifications. The coordinate sum in the definition alone does not assert C1. In later theorem statements, T1–T5 and C1 are explicitly listed as hypotheses; they are not treated as established physical laws.

def-tdmath-forward-signed-comparison.title: Signed comparison for forward-sector relations

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, §II.D
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §4.1, complete 607-page edition

def-tdmath-forward-signed-comparison.statement: Let $u,v$ be finite-support real coefficient maps on the tagged state labels of [[def-tdmath-tagged-scalable-compound]] with equal total coefficient. For a typed state $x$, compound notation uses the represented map $\mathsf{J}(x)$ from [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]]; its raw unit point mass is $e_{(\Gamma,x)}$. Signed maps still use the ordinary total of their raw coefficients, exactly the bookkeeping mass of the represented nonnegative maps. Put $d=v-u$, $d^+(x)=\max(d(x),0)$ and $d^-(x)=\max(-d(x),0)$. Define $u\preceq_s v$ to mean $d^-\prec d^+$ under the compound relation of [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]]. Write $u\sim_s v$ when both $u\preceq_s v$ and $v\preceq_s u$. These are formal signed comparison maps, not physical negative amounts. The positive and negative parts are finite-support compounds of equal mass. If $u\sim_s v$, then $cu\sim_s cv$ for every real $c$: positive $c$ uses scaling, $c=0$ is reflexivity, and negative $c$ swaps the positive and negative parts while equivalence supplies both comparison directions. This Definition introduces the signed notation; ordinary-order compatibility and the signed-order laws are proved separately.

lem-tdmath-reference-strip-coordinate.title: A unique reference coordinate inside a thermal strip

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, §IV.B.1, pp. 54–56
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapter 4, complete 607-page edition

lem-tdmath-reference-strip-coordinate.statement: Let a simple domain and its finite thermal joins satisfy [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]] and [[def-tdmath-thermal-contact-hypotheses]]. Let $x_0\prec\prec x_1$ with $x_0\sim_T x_1$, and let $x$ satisfy $x_0\prec\prec x\prec\prec x_1$. For $0\le\lambda\le1$, write $R_\lambda$ for the compound state $((1-\lambda)x_0,\lambda x_1)$, omitting a zero coefficient at the endpoints. Then there is a unique $\lambda\in(0,1)$ with $R_\lambda\sim x$ in the common accessibility relation.

thm-tdmath-reference-strip-gluing.title: Reference-strip gluing proves comparison for scaled copies

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, Theorem 4.4 and Lemma 4.1, pp. 54–56
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapters 2 and 4, complete 607-page edition

thm-tdmath-reference-strip-gluing.statement: Assume [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]] and T1–T4 of [[def-tdmath-thermal-contact-hypotheses]] for every finite join. For any one simple type $\Gamma_i$, every two finite compounds of its scaled copies with the same total coefficient mass are comparable. Thus CH holds on all multiple scaled products of that type. No entropy across different material types is asserted here.

thm-tdmath-conditional-contact-calibrato.title: Contact calibrators under explicit join coherence

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, Theorems 4.5–4.8, pp. 55–59
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapters 2 and 4, complete 607-page edition

thm-tdmath-conditional-contact-calibrato.statement:
Let $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2$ be simple domains in a family of finite thermal joins satisfying A1–A7, S1–S3, T1–T5, and C1 of [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]] and [[def-tdmath-thermal-contact-hypotheses]]. Then there are $x_0\prec\prec x_1$ in $\Gamma_1$ and $y_0\prec\prec y_1$ in $\Gamma_2$ such that

$$(x_0,y_1)\sim(x_1,y_0).$$

Moreover, for every fixed finite composition of scaled copies of $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$, any two equal-mass states of that same composition are comparable (CH). The conclusion is conditional on the explicitly stated join-coherence and universal-range assumptions C1 and T5.

thm-tdmath-arbitrary-family-calibration.title: Calibration of an arbitrary family of simple-system entropies

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, Theorem 2.5 and §IV.B.2, pp. 27–29, 56–59
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapters 2 and 4, complete 607-page edition

thm-tdmath-arbitrary-family-calibration.statement:
Let $I$ be a nonempty set of primitive simple-system labels containing a distinguished meter label $m$. Assume every finite separated product is explicitly represented by its finitely many tagged elementary factors; positive scaling and finite product are the only identifications. Suppose the join-closed family satisfies the hypotheses of [[thm-tdmath-conditional-contact-calibrator]], and fix a strict meter pair $z_0\prec\prec z_1$ in $\Gamma_m$. Assume the Axiom of Choice. Then one can choose, for every $i\in I$, an additive constant and positive scale for its same-type entropy so that

$$S\big((t_1i_1,x_1),\ldots,(t_ni_n,x_n)\big)=\sum_{\ell=1}^n t_\ell S_{i_\ell}(x_\ell)$$

is additive, extensive, and characterizes every same-composition comparison on every finite separated product. No conclusion is asserted for transitions that change composition.

ex-tdmath-logarithmic-coherence-witness.title: Logarithmic contact model with coherent joins

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, §§III–IV, pp. 37–59
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapters 2 and 4, complete 607-page edition

ex-tdmath-logarithmic-coherence-witness.statement:
Let $I$ be a finite nonempty set of primitive labels, choose $c_i,r_i,u_i^*,v_i^*>0$ and $b_i\in\mathbb R$ for each $i\in I$, and use the positive state domain $\Gamma_i=(0,\infty)^2$ with coordinates $(U,V)$. Close these tags under positive scaling, finite separated products, and finite thermal joins, retaining all constituent tags. The reference scales $u_i^*,v_i^*$ have the same respective units as $U,V$; write $\ln$ for the natural logarithm $\log$ of [[def-natural-logarithm]]. Thus every logarithm argument is dimensionless. For a unit amount set $\sigma_i(U,V)=c_i\ln(U/u_i^*)+r_i\ln(V/v_i^*)+b_i$. For any amount $t>0$, define on the scaled type $ti$

$$\sigma_{ti}(U,V)=tc_i\ln\!\left(\frac{U}{tu_i^*}\right)+tr_i\ln\!\left(\frac{V}{tv_i^*}\right)+tb_i.$$

For a separated finite product, add component entropies. For a thermal join of a finite nonempty list of components indexed $j=1,\ldots,m$, write $\alpha_j=t_jc_{i_j}$, $\beta_j=t_jr_{i_j}$, $d_j=t_ju_{i_j}^*$, $e_j=t_jv_{i_j}^*$, and $C=\sum_j\alpha_j>0$. Define its entropy at total energy $U>0$ and positive work coordinates $V_j$ by

$$\sigma_J(U,V_1,\ldots,V_m)=\sum_{j=1}^m\alpha_j\ln\!\left(\frac{\alpha_jU}{Cd_j}\right)+\sum_{j=1}^m\beta_j\ln\!\left(\frac{V_j}{e_j}\right)+\sum_{j=1}^mt_jb_{i_j}.$$

Give each primitive generator its unit amount vector; scaled and joined types retain all primitive amounts, and let $w_T$ be their sum, with $w_{tT}=tw_T$ and joined weight equal to the sum of component weights. Use the represented state $\mathsf{J}_T(x)=w_T e_{(T,x)}$ from [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]]. For a finite encoded map $c$, define its entropy by the finite sum $\sigma(c)=\sum_{(T,x)}c(T,x)\sigma_T(x)/w_T$, omitting zero terms. Its aggregate composition is the corresponding amount-vector sum from that supplier. Thus $\sigma(\mathsf{J}_T(x))=\sigma_T(x)$, while a raw unit point mass has entropy $\sigma_T(x)/w_T$. Scaled and joined raw tags are distinct; the displayed formulas make their declared preparation transport entropy-preserving.

On every finite compound of these closed tagged types, define accessibility by nondecrease of this entropy across states of the same composition, including the separated and joined representations of a contact. This is a mathematical consistency model; it is not an observed gas experiment or a universal thermodynamic assertion.

pthm-td-contact-product-comparison.title: Conditional contact calibrator and product comparison
pthm-td-contact-product-comparison.physical_scope: Conditional consequence of the adopted A1–A7, S1–S3, T1–T5 and C1 assumptions for the declared finite thermal-contact family; not an unconditional law for real materials.

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, Theorem 4.8 and §§IV.A–IV.C
André Thess, The Lieb–Yngvason Machine: A didactical tool for the definition of entropy in classical thermodynamics, §§2–4
Goddard, The second law of thermodynamics as variation on a theme of Carathéodory, §§2–3

pthm-td-contact-product-comparison.statement:
For every declared finite family of simple-system domains closed under the thermal joins of [[def-td-thermal-join]], assume the accessibility axioms A1–A6, the simple-system assumptions A7 and S1–S3, the contact assumptions T1–T4, the universal thermal-equilibrium range T5, and equilibrium-join coherence C1, with the exact formulations in [[post-td-accessibility-a1-a6]], [[post-td-simple-system-geometric-axioms]], [[post-td-thermal-join-axioms]], [[post-td-universal-thermal-range]], and [[post-td-equilibrium-join-coherence]]. Then for any two simple types $i,j$, there are $x_0\prec\prec x_1$ in $i$ and $y_0\prec\prec y_1$ in $j$ such that

$$ (x_0,y_1)\sim(x_1,y_0). $$

Moreover, for this fixed pair $i,j$, every finite separated product made only from positive scaled copies of $i$ and $j$ satisfies the comparison hypothesis: any two equal-formal-mass states $A,B$ of that product type satisfy $A\prec B$ or $B\prec A$. No comparison conclusion for products involving a third primitive type is contained in this pairwise result. These are conditional model deductions. In particular, the conclusion is not claimed from the printed Theorem 4.8 interface with T1–T4 alone; the local mathematical supplier explicitly requires the additional T5 and C1 branch.

thm-tdmath-interval-event-ensemble-limit.title: Interacting density-interval and upper-energy event limit

references.title: H.-O. Georgii, Large deviations and the equivalence of ensembles for Gibbsian particle systems with superstable interaction
references.locator: Theorem 4 and Sections 5–7, printed pp.177–195 / PDF pp.7–25: density interval with upper energy event, entropy minimizers and finite multiplier.

references.title: H.-O. Georgii and H. Zessin, Large deviations and the maximum entropy principle for marked point random fields
references.locator: Sections 3 and 5, printed pp.188–195 and 197–204: entropy upper/lower event estimates and conditional laws.

thm-tdmath-interval-event-ensemble-limit.statement:
Assume the superstable regular model and Poisson conventions of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]]. Let $D\subset[0,\infty)$ be an interval of positive length, let $\nu$ be the supremum of finite-entropy, finite-energy attainable densities, and set $e_0(\rho)=\inf\{\Phi(P):\rho(P)=\rho,\ I(P)<\infty\}$. If $\inf D<\nu$ and $e>\inf_{\rho\in D}e_0(\rho)$, define
$$A_L=\{N_{\Lambda_L}/L^d\in D,\ H_{L,\mathrm{per}}/L^d\leq e\}.$$
Then $A_L$ has positive Poisson probability for all sufficiently large $L$, and
$$\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Q_{\Lambda_L}(A_L) =-\min\{I(P):\rho(P)\in\overline D,\ \Phi(P)\leq e\}.$$
Let $R_{L,\omega}$ be the periodized empirical field of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]]. There are $\beta\geq0$ and $z>0$ such that the empirical fields under the conditional law $Q_{\Lambda_L}(\cdot\mid A_L)$ and the matching periodic grand-canonical law concentrate in every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood of the common minimizer set of $I+\beta\Phi-\rho\log z$ when $\beta>0$. At $\beta=0$, retain the forbidden-pair set $B=\{x:\phi(x)=+\infty\}$ and use $I-\rho\log z$ on the hard-admissible stationary class $\mathcal K_B$, with grand weight $z^N\mathbf1_{\rm admissible}$; no value is assigned to $0\cdot(+\infty)$. If this minimizer is unique, both empirical fields converge to it in probability in $\tau_L$. These are empirical-field conclusions. The periodically continued conditional and grand laws also converge in $\tau_L$ under the same uniqueness assumption, for all measurable local observables of at-most-linear count growth. The energy constraint is an upper event and $D$ is nondegenerate; this does not assert exact $N$, a shrinking shell, or a singular energy surface.

thm-tdmath-retained-hard-zero-beta-limit.title: Zero-inverse-temperature-parameter limit with forbidden pairs retained

references.title: H.-O. Georgii, Large deviations and the equivalence of ensembles for Gibbsian particle systems with superstable interaction
references.locator: Section 2 finite-volume Gibbs weights for potentials taking +infinity, printed pp.172–174 / PDF pp.2–4. Theorem 4 permits a zero energy multiplier; the explicitly retained-admissibility partition branch and its local-limit entropy argument are developed here.

references.title: H.-O. Georgii and H. Zessin, Large deviations and the maximum entropy principle for marked point random fields
references.locator: Sections 2.3, 3, and 5: Poisson-reference entropy, compactness and block comparisons used in the local proof.

thm-tdmath-retained-hard-zero-beta-limit.statement:
Let $\phi$ be superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and let $B=\{x:\phi(x)=+\infty\}$. For a finite configuration $\omega$, call it admissible when no pair displacement belongs to $B$; for periodic boxes require this also for every periodic image pair. Define the zero-inverse-temperature-parameter continuation (the mathematical $\beta=0$ branch) to be $z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf 1_{\rm admissible}(\omega)$, explicitly retaining the hard exclusion. Then the normalized Poisson free and periodic partition rates exist and equal
$$-\min_{P\in\mathcal K_B}\{I(P)-\rho(P)\log z\},$$
where $\mathcal K_B$ is the set of stationary laws with no forbidden pair almost surely. The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in $\tau_L$. The periodically continued grand laws are relatively compact in $\tau_L$, all their accumulation points are minimizers, and if this minimizer is unique they converge to it for every measurable local observable of at-most-linear count growth. If $B=\varnothing$, this is the Poisson activity-$z$ model. For $B\ne\varnothing$, it is not an unrestricted Poisson law and does not assign a value to the undefined product $0\cdot(+\infty)$.

pthm-td-controlled-continuum-thermodynam.title: Controlled continuum interval-energy thermodynamic limit
pthm-td-controlled-continuum-thermodynam.physical_scope: Superstable regular classical positional pair systems in periodic cubes at positive temperature, together with the expressly defined formal retained-hard-admissibility zero-inverse-temperature branch, with a nondegenerate density interval and strict upper-energy threshold; periodically continued local convergence requires the stated unique minimizer.

references.title: Hans-Otto Georgii, Large deviations and the equivalence of ensembles for Gibbsian particle systems with superstable interaction, Probability Theory and Related Fields 99 (1994), 171–195
David Tong, Statistical Physics (author-hosted Cambridge lecture notes)
Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part SM: Statistical Mechanics (2024 author-hosted lecture notes)

pthm-td-controlled-continuum-thermodynam.statement:
Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB, as required by the current variational-pressure supplier. Let $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$, $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$, and assume $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable. Require the exact superstable regular hypotheses of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]] for this dimensionless potential: a stable part plus a nonnegative core part bounded below by a positive constant on an $\ell^\infty$-ball, with the supplier's lower and upper regular tail conditions. Use $\widehat H=H/E_0$, $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta$ for $\beta>0$, and $\widehat e=e/E_0$; then $\beta H=\widehat\beta\widehat H$. For this supplier convention, let $\nu$ be the supremum of finite-entropy, finite-energy attainable densities for $\widehat\varphi$, and write $\widehat\Phi(P)$ for the supplier's limiting positional energy density; let $e_0(\rho)=\inf\{\widehat\Phi(P):\rho(P)=\rho,\ I(P)<\infty\}$ be its numerical positional-energy infimum. Let $D\subset[0,\infty)$ be a nondegenerate density interval, and require $\inf D<\nu$ and $\widehat e>\inf_{\rho\in D}e_0(\rho)$. Use periodic boxes and the density-interval/upper-energy conditional preparation. For $\beta>0$, the finite-volume grand and microcanonical weights are those of [[post-td-equilibrium-ensemble-sampling]]. For $\beta=0$, require a nonempty hard-core displacement set and use the formal retained-admissibility continuation of [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]]; do not interpret $0\cdot(+\infty)$.

For both the positive-$\beta$ branch and the formal retained-hard-core $\beta=0$ branch, [[thm-tdmath-interval-event-ensemble-limit]] gives eventual event positivity, the constrained entropy-rate limit, and common-minimizer accumulation points; at $\beta=0$, [[thm-tdmath-retained-hard-zero-beta-limit]] identifies the matching retained grand law and minimizer set. If the relevant common minimizer set is the singleton adopted in [[post-td-grand-variational-phase-uniqueness]] for the multiplier pair supplied by that branch, both the conditioned laws and the corresponding periodic grand laws converge locally to $P^\ast$ for every measurable local observable $f$ with $|f|\leq c(1+N_A)$ on a bounded region $A$. This is an interval-density and upper-energy result, not a fixed-particle-number or shrinking-shell theorem.


Here local observables are evaluated on the periodic continuation of the prepared torus configuration. This is the same periodic boundary preparation, with no new physical sampling assumption; a configuration is not extended by the empty configuration outside its fundamental cube.

pthm-td-interacting-three-ensemble-local.title: Interacting exact-N shrinking-shell three-ensemble local limit
pthm-td-interacting-three-ensemble-local.physical_scope: Superstable regular classical positional Borel pair systems in periodic boxes, at positive temperature and interior density, with differentiable canonical rate and a singleton grand variational minimizer; local observables use the same periodic continuation, and kinetic momentum is excluded.

references.title: Hans-Otto Georgii, Large deviations and the equivalence of ensembles for Gibbsian particle systems with superstable interaction, Probability Theory and Related Fields 99 (1994), 171–195
David Tong, Statistical Physics (author-hosted Cambridge lecture notes)
Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part SM: Statistical Mechanics (2024 author-hosted lecture notes)

pthm-td-interacting-three-ensemble-local.statement:
Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB as required by the current variational-pressure supplier. Let $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$, $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$, and assume $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable. Require the exact superstable regular hypotheses of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]; use $\widehat H=H/E_0$ and $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta>0$ in its mathematical suppliers. Let $F(\rho,\beta)$ denote the numerical canonical rate evaluated at $\widehat\beta$; assume it is differentiable in physical $\beta$ at the chosen temperature and set $e=-\partial_\beta F(\rho,\beta)$, in joules per dimensionless reference volume. For periodic cubes $\Lambda_n$, take exact particle numbers $N_n$ with $N_n/V_n\to\rho$ at a positive interior attainable density. Choose a finite supporting activity parameter $\alpha$ for $F$ at $\rho$ and set $z=e^\alpha>0$; assume the corresponding stationary grand variational minimizer is the singleton $P^\ast$ as in [[post-td-grand-variational-phase-uniqueness]].

Then there exists a constructed sequence $\delta_n\downarrow0$ for which the periodic exact-$N_n$ canonical positional law, the periodic grand-canonical law at $(\alpha,\beta)$, and the uniform positional shell law of [[def-td-controlled-fixed-n-energy-shell]] on
$$N=N_n,\qquad |H_{N_n}^{\mathrm{per}}/V_n-e|\leq\delta_n$$
all converge locally to $P^\ast$. Convergence means convergence of expectations for every measurable local observable $f$ supported in a bounded region and satisfying $|f|\leq c(1+N_A)$ there. The shell sequence is constructed from canonical concentration; arbitrary preassigned shrinking widths, exact zero-width surfaces, full phase-space shells involving kinetic momentum, and a conclusion at nonunique minimizers are not asserted.

Here local observables are evaluated on the periodic continuation of the prepared torus configuration. This is the same periodic boundary preparation, with no new physical sampling assumption; a configuration is not extended by the empty configuration outside its fundamental cube.

lem-tdmath-periodic-law-local-tame-trans.title: Periodic preparation and local-tame transfer from entropy bounds

references.title: H.-O. Georgii, Large deviations and the equivalence of ensembles for Gibbsian particle systems with superstable interaction

lem-tdmath-periodic-law-local-tame-trans.statement:
Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB as in [[thm-tdmath-local-tame-entropy-compactness]]. Let $L\to\infty$ and let $C_L$ be probability laws on finite configurations in $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, invariant under every translation modulo $L\mathbb Z^d$. Write $Q_L$ for unit-intensity Poisson measure and suppose
$$c_L=L^{-d}D(C_L\Vert Q_L),\qquad \sup_L c_L<\infty.$$
Let $\widetilde C_L$ be the law of the periodic continuation. Then $\widetilde C_L=E_{C_L}R_{L,\omega}$; these laws are stationary and are relatively sequentially compact in $\tau_L$ as $L\to\infty$. Their local counts are uniformly integrable. Along any convergent subsequence with limit $P$,
$$I(P)\leq\liminf_L c_L.$$
If the empirical fields $R_{L,\omega}$ converge in probability in $\tau_L$ to a fixed $P_*$, then $\widetilde C_L\to P_*$ in $\tau_L$, including expectations of every measurable local $f$ with $|f|\leq b(1+N_A)$ for bounded $A$. This concerns periodic continuation, not the zero extension of a configuration outside its fundamental cube.
